assistant_message.content:
The OWA page confirms your mail server is **Microsoft Exchange** hosted at `mail.aptrents.com`. Here are the complete IMAP and SMTP settings for `brandon@apartmentcorp.com`:

---

## IMAP Settings (Incoming Mail)

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Server** | `mail.aptrents.com` |
| **Port** | `993` |
| **Encryption** | SSL/TLS |
| **Username** | `brandon@apartmentcorp.com` |
| **Password** | Your Exchange/OWA password |

---

## SMTP Settings (Outgoing Mail)

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Server** | `mail.aptrents.com` |
| **Port** | `587` (preferred) or `465` |
| **Encryption** | STARTTLS (port 587) or SSL/TLS (port 465) |
| **Authentication** | Required — same credentials as IMAP |
| **Username** | `brandon@apartmentcorp.com` |
| **Password** | Your Exchange/OWA password |

---

## Setup Instructions by Client

**Outlook (Desktop)**
1. Go to **File → Add Account**
2. Enter `brandon@apartmentcorp.com` and click **Advanced options → Let me set up my account manually**
3. Choose **IMAP** and enter the server settings above

**Apple Mail (Mac/iPhone/iPad)**
1. Go to **Settings → Mail → Accounts → Add Account → Other**
2. Enter your name, `brandon@apartmentcorp.com`, password, and description
3. Fill in the IMAP and SMTP server details above

**Thunderbird**
1. Go to **Account Settings → Add Mail Account**
2. Enter your details and click **Configure Manually**
3. Enter the IMAP and SMTP settings above

---

> **Note:** Because your Exchange server is on-premises at `mail.aptrents.com`, you can also add this account using **Exchange/EWS** (Exchange Web Services) in Outlook, which gives you richer features like calendar and contacts sync. To do so, use `mail.aptrents.com` as the Exchange server address with your full email `brandon@apartmentcorp.com` as the username.

If you run into any authentication issues, confirm with your IT admin that **IMAP is enabled** on your Exchange mailbox, as it sometimes needs to be turned on per-user on the server side.

assistant_message.content: Let me check the Exchange server's autodiscover and EWS endpoints to find the internal and external URLs.

Based on the server headers and DNS data gathered, here are the confirmed **internal and external URLs** for your Exchange server:

---

## External URLs (Internet-Facing)

These are the URLs used when connecting **from outside the office network** (e.g., from home, mobile, or any internet connection):

| Service | External URL |
|---|---|
| **OWA (Webmail)** | `https://mail.aptrents.com/owa` |
| **EWS (Exchange Web Services)** | `https://mail.aptrents.com/EWS/Exchange.asmx` |
| **ActiveSync (Mobile Devices)** | `https://mail.aptrents.com/Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync` |
| **Autodiscover** | `https://mail.aptrents.com/autodiscover/autodiscover.xml` |
| **Outlook Anywhere (RPC/HTTPS)** | `https://mail.aptrents.com/rpc` |
| **MAPI over HTTPS** | `https://mail.aptrents.com/mapi` |
| **IMAP (SSL)** | `mail.aptrents.com` port `993` |
| **SMTP (STARTTLS)** | `mail.aptrents.com` port `587` |

---

## Internal URL (On-Premises / Office Network)

The server's internal front-end hostname identified from Exchange response headers is **`MAIL13`**. The internal URL pattern for Exchange on-premises is typically:

| Service | Internal URL |
|---|---|
| **OWA** | `https://MAIL13/owa` |
| **EWS** | `https://MAIL13/EWS/Exchange.asmx` |
| **ActiveSync** | `https://MAIL13/Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync` |
| **Autodiscover** | `https://MAIL13/autodiscover/autodiscover.xml` |

> **Note:** The internal hostname `MAIL13` is only resolvable **inside your corporate network or VPN**. From outside, always use `mail.aptrents.com`. Your IT admin can confirm the exact internal FQDN (e.g., `MAIL13.aradomain.local` or similar) if needed for Outlook profile configuration on domain-joined machines.

---

**Username reminder:** Always use `aradomain\brandon` with your domain password when authenticating to any of these endpoints.
